title: Microsoft's Copilot Cowork goes live, and SpaceX buys Cursor
excerpt: Microsoft's agent-style Copilot Cowork is now generally available, SpaceX agreed to buy the coding tool Cursor for $60 billion, and AI costs are changing how people work.

items.t: Microsoft announced that Copilot Cowork is now generally available. The Microsoft 365 Copilot app now includes a toggle that takes you into Cowork's full experience, so you can "move from chat to action".

items.h: SpaceX to acquire the AI coding startup Cursor
items.t: CNBC reported that SpaceX, which merged with Elon Musk's AI company xAI earlier this year, will acquire Cursor for $60 billion. CNBC adds that Anthropic now controls half of the AI coding category.

items.h: Tech workers move from using AI as much as possible to using it carefully
items.t: The New York Times reported that tech workers who "maxed out" their AI use are now trying to minimise it, as the cost of usage (counted in "tokens") adds up.

items.h: The rising cost of AI in Africa
items.t: The Guardian Nigeria published an opinion piece, "Priced out of the future", on the rising cost of AI in Africa.

water.t: The Information reported in its newsletter that Google and Microsoft are teaming up to push back against Anthropic and OpenAI. The article is behind a paywall, so details are limited.

means.t: Agents like Cowork do tasks, not just answer questions. Learn to brief one: the goal, the background, what "done" looks like, and what it must not do. A clear brief is the whole skill.
AI has a running cost. Use the free tiers first, keep prompts short and reuse saved context (projects, custom instructions) instead of pasting the same background every time.
Tools change owners quickly. Keep your client workflow tool-agnostic: your prompts, templates and checks should survive a change of app.

prompt: Write a one-page brief for an AI agent. Goal: [what you want done]. Background: [why and for whom]. Done looks like: [exact output]. Rules: public information only; do not send, buy or delete anything; ask me before any action that cannot be undone. When finished, list what you did and what you are unsure about.
